grading.ungraded_reason: no linked order package / not in the action's closed_only delta
grading.reading: 67 of 89 are C, but that is largely 'not enough recorded to grade', not a verdict: entry_quality is `unknown` for every pairs leg (no confidence recorded on that path) and risk_management is `unknown` for ALL 89. The single D (ict_scalp_sol_15m, conf 0.28, entry=should_skip) then returned +8.96R - the grade scores the DECISION, not the outcome.
grading.grader_defect_caveat: ⚠️ EVERY GRADE IN THIS REPORT CARRIES A KNOWN DEFECT, confirmed in my OWN output today. BL-20260821-GRADER-CALLS-A-RECONCILER-CLOSE-A-TAKE-PROFIT says the grader labels exit_quality from the R VALUE rather than the exit MECHANISM. My 89 fresh grades reproduce it verbatim: `exit=tp_appropriate(reconciler_filled,1.03R)`, `exit=tp_appropriate(netting_attributed,12.81R)`, and — most clearly — `exit=tp_appropriate(sl,0.76R)`, which grades a STOP-LOSS exit as an appropriate TAKE-PROFIT because the R came out positive. So the exit_quality axis of these grades is not trustworthy; entry_quality and the decision_grade are unaffected.

cross_review_notes.note: THE ALARM CHANNEL WAS REPAIRED IN THIS WINDOW - report it as a win, with the population. Over 394 ERROR+ rows spanning 2026-08-20T14:28Z -> 2026-08-29T14:05Z (limit=1000, so NOT limit-truncated), two known floods are 333 rows = 84.5%: ict_scalp_mgc no-candle 225 and ib_target_naked 108. BOTH STOPPED. Daily ERROR+ went 30/48/95/49/72/63 (08-20..25) -> 11/9/15/2 (08-26..29): ~59.5/day -> ~9.25/day, an 84% reduction. The transient classifier fix and the durable target-naked cooldown are EXERCISED, not merely deployed.

BUT THE CLASSIFIER FIX MOVED THE MGC CONDITION, IT DID NOT CURE IT. The same condition now appears at WARN, correctly labelled transient_market_data_unavailable: 38 rows for ict_scalp_mgc_15m continuing through 08-27/28/29. BROKER TRUTH IS 47 DAYS STALE AND SAYS WORSE THAN THE JOURNAL. comms/broker_truth_ledger.json carries one record: bybit_2 realized -$262.52 as of 2026-07-13, ~8x the journal's figure. It is populated BY HAND from a venue export, so the absence of records for every other account means nobody has reconciled them - NOT that they reconcile. /performance journalTrust correctly reports accountsKnownDivergent: ['bybit_2'].

A FOURTH CORRECTION TO MY OWN OUTPUT, found after the report was first rendered and fixed in the same run. 513 timestamps I wrote into docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json were dated in the FUTURE — the triage batches carry `at` / `resolved_at` values from 17:15Z to 18:20Z, while `date -u` at the time of the check read 17:17Z and the commits that introduced them are stamped 16:47:02 through 17:06:59. So the record asserted observations at times that had not happened, on up to 455 rows. The performance and ml backlogs are clean (0 future stamps), which is the positive control that says this was a bad clock in one pass rather than a systematic habit. FIXED, not annotated: each fake value was mapped back to the AUTHOR TIME of the specific commit that introduced it, derived empirically by diffing each triage commit against its parent rather than guessed — 17:15->16:47:02 (58b81b7), 17:25 and 17:35->16:53:04 (ff37907), 17:45->16:55:45 (d691542), 17:55->16:59:08 (259fc50), 18:05->17:02:42 (702176e), 18:15 and 18:20->17:06:59 (f8fe620). Every stamp is now verifiable against git rather than against my assertion. The batch shares one value per commit, which is honest: the rows in a batch were written together and I cannot reconstruct per-row times, so a shared true timestamp is the most precision the evidence supports. Recorded here because a triage note's whole value is that it says WHEN a row was last re-validated, and a future date makes that claim unfalsifiable.
